scientific_question: Does a project-held-out activation-trained entry-state score predict realized positive transit speed when route geometry is controlled by exact directed station-pair fixed effects?

score.boundary: score weights exclude held-out-project migration outcomes; predictor preprocessing remains panel-derived

segment_definition.source_rows: public source migration_*.csv files for the six focal projects
include_if: eel is an expert-corrected initiator (the nine fixed 2015 expert non-migrants are excluded)
immediately preceding row for the same fish migration == TRUE
previous and current station_name are nonempty and different

primary_model.fish_weighting: inverse of included segment count per fish so each fish contributes total weight 1
primary_model.inference: cluster-robust sandwich SE by fish with finite-sample CR1 correction
primary_model.estimand: multiplicative transit-speed ratio per 1 SD entry-state score

interpretation.positive_supported: entry state retains a local realized-transit component that was hidden by individual-level speed aggregation
interpretation.null_compatible: entry state is informative for migratory commitment/onset but not for realized motion speed even within the same route links
interpretation.negative_supported: higher entry state predicts slower realized transit within identical links; do not interpret as lower intrinsic capacity without further mechanism data

prohibitions: do not retune pair-support thresholds after seeing the primary coefficient
do not drop extreme positive source speeds after inspecting their association with score
do not treat segment rows as independent fish
do not call a null coefficient proof that physiology is irrelevant after activation

fixed_provenance_rule.expert_corrections: Exclude the nine fixed 2015 expert-classified non-migrants used in every canonical activation/post-activation analysis, even if source rows contain migration==TRUE.
fixed_provenance_rule.rationale: This rule predates the within-link result and defines the canonical activated population; its omission from the first within-link implementation was an implementation bug, not an outcome-driven eligibility change.
